knowledge:
- key_parameters: splicedAlignment=Set to TRUE in qAlign to enable spliced alignments for RNA-seq (using HISAT2) ;; aligner=Specifies the alignment tool in qAlign (e.g., "Rhisat2" or "Rbowtie") ;; bisulfite=Set to "dir" (directional) or "undir" (undirectional) in qAlign to enable bisulfite-specific alignment ;; maxHits=Maximum number of alignments allowed per read (e.g., set to 50 for miRNA-seq to capture multi-mapping reads) ;; snpFile=Path to a tab-delimited file containing SNPs for allele-specific alignment ;; reportLevel=Controls quantification level in qCount ("gene", "exon", or "junction") ;; includeSpliced=Set to FALSE in qCount to exclude spliced alignments when counting exon body alignments ;; orientation=Specifies read orientation relative to query regions in qCount or qProfile ("same", "opposite", or "any") ;; mode=Specifies the methylation context/combination mode in qMeth (e.g., "CpGcomb")
- alternatives: Rhisat2 vs Rbowtie=Use Rhisat2 (with splicedAlignment=TRUE) for spliced RNA-seq alignments, and Rbowtie for unspliced alignments (ChIP-seq, Bis-seq, miRNA-seq) ;; SpliceMap=An older spliced aligner previously supported by QuasR, but Rhisat2 is now recommended ;; Downstream statistical packages=Count tables generated by qCount can be passed directly to edgeR, DESeq, DESeq2, TCC, DEXSeq, or baySeq for differential analysis
- when_to_use: Use when performing complete workflows (preprocessing, alignment, QC, and quantification) for single-end or paired-end ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, Bis-seq, or smRNA-seq datasets within the R environment.
- pitfalls: Redundant genomes=BSgenome packages like BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19 (newer than 1.4.0) and BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38 contain redundant alternative variant sequences, causing reads to be wrongly classified as multi-mapping; use "analysis set" or "primary assembly" versions instead ;; Deleting parameter files=Do not delete the .txt parameter files generated alongside .bam files, as qAlign relies on them to verify and reuse existing alignments ;; Sample consistency=All samples within a project must be of the same type (e.g., mixing single-end and paired-end, or fasta and fastq files in a single sample file is not allowed) ;; miRNA multi-mapping=miRNA reads often map to multiple genomic loci; using the default maxHits=1 will underestimate their expression, so maxHits should be set to a higher value (e.g., 50) ;; External BAM files=When using externally generated BAM files, ensure they contain only one alignment per read to satisfy the counting assumptions of qCount

workflows.name: chip_seq_workflow
workflows.intent: Align single-end ChIP-seq reads, perform quality control, export coverage tracks, and quantify alignments at promoters and TSS profiles.
input: samples_chip_single.txt (tab-delimited sample file listing raw fastq files and sample names)
workflows.stages: 1. Align reads to genome and auxiliary targets using qAlign. ;; 2. Generate quality control report using qQCReport. ;; 3. Retrieve alignment statistics using alignmentStats. ;; 4. Export coverage tracks to wiggle format using qExportWig. ;; 5. Quantify promoter region counts using qCount. ;; 6. Calculate average alignment profiles around TSS using qProfile.
workflows.code:
sampleFile <- "extdata/samples_chip_single.txt"
auxFile <- "extdata/auxiliaries.txt"
genomeFile <- "extdata/hg19sub.fa"

proj1 <- qAlign(sampleFile, genome = genomeFile, auxiliaryFile = auxFile)
proj1

qQCReport(proj1, pdfFilename = "extdata/qc_report.pdf")

alignmentStats(proj1)

qExportWig(proj1, binsize = 100L, scaling = TRUE, collapseBySample = TRUE)

library(txdbmaker)
annotFile <- "extdata/hg19sub_annotation.gtf"
chrLen <- scanFaIndex(genomeFile)
chrominfo <- data.frame(chrom = as.character(seqnames(chrLen)),
                        length = width(chrLen),
                        is_circular = rep(FALSE, length(chrLen)))
txdb <- makeTxDbFromGFF(file = annotFile, format = "gtf",
                        chrominfo = chrominfo,
                        dataSource = "Ensembl",
                        organism = "Homo sapiens")
promReg <- promoters(txdb, upstream = 1000, downstream = 500,
                     columns = c("gene_id","tx_id"))
gnId <- vapply(mcols(promReg)$gene_id,
               FUN = paste, FUN.VALUE = "",
               collapse = ",")
promRegSel <- promReg[ match(unique(gnId), gnId) ]
names(promRegSel) <- unique(gnId)

cnt <- qCount(proj1, promRegSel)
cnt

library(rtracklayer)
annotationFile <- "extdata/hg19sub_annotation.gtf"
tssRegions <- import.gff(annotationFile, format = "gtf",
                         feature.type = "start_codon",
                         colnames = "gene_name")
tssRegions <- tssRegions[!duplicated(tssRegions)]
names(tssRegions) <- rep("TSS", length(tssRegions))

prS <- qProfile(proj1, tssRegions, upstream = 3000, downstream = 3000, 
                orientation = "same")
prO <- qProfile(proj1, tssRegions, upstream = 3000, downstream = 3000, 
                orientation = "opposite")

workflows.name: rna_seq_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform spliced alignment of RNA-seq reads and quantify expression at gene, exon, and junction levels.
input: samples_rna_paired.txt (tab-delimited sample file listing paired-end fastq files)
workflows.stages: 1. Align paired-end reads with spliced alignment enabled using qAlign. ;; 2. Quantify gene and exon expression levels using qCount. ;; 3. Quantify exon-exon junctions using qCount with reportLevel="junction". ;; 4. Quantify exon body levels excluding spliced alignments using qCount with includeSpliced=FALSE.
workflows.code:
file.copy(system.file(package = "QuasR", "extdata"), ".", recursive = TRUE)

sampleFile <- "extdata/samples_rna_paired.txt"
genomeFile <- "extdata/hg19sub.fa"

proj2 <- qAlign(sampleFile, genome = genomeFile,
                splicedAlignment = TRUE, aligner = "Rhisat2")
proj2

geneLevels <- qCount(proj2, txdb, reportLevel = "gene")
exonLevels <- qCount(proj2, txdb, reportLevel = "exon")

geneRPKM <- t(t(geneLevels[,-1] / geneLevels[,1] * 1000)
              / colSums(geneLevels[,-1]) * 1e6)

exonJunctions <- qCount(proj2, NULL, reportLevel = "junction")

exonBodyLevels <- qCount(proj2, txdb, reportLevel = "exon",
                         includeSpliced = FALSE)

workflows.name: mirna_seq_workflow
workflows.intent: Preprocess small RNA reads by trimming adapters, align them allowing multi-mapping, and quantify mature and primary miRNAs.
input: samples_mirna.txt (tab-delimited sample file listing raw miRNA fasta files)
workflows.stages: 1. Trim 3' library adapters from raw reads using preprocessReads. ;; 2. Align processed reads allowing multi-mapping (high maxHits) using qAlign. ;; 3. Import miRNA annotations and define extended query windows around mature miRNA 5' ends. ;; 4. Quantify mature and primary miRNAs using qCount.
workflows.code:
sampleFile <- file.path("extdata", "samples_mirna.txt")
sampleFile2 <- sub(".txt", "_processed.txt", sampleFile)

tab <- read.delim(sampleFile, header = TRUE, as.is = TRUE)
tab2 <- tab
tab2$FileName <- sub(".fa", "_processed.fa", tab$FileName)
write.table(tab2, sampleFile2, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

oldwd <- setwd(dirname(sampleFile))
res <- preprocessReads(tab$FileName,
                       tab2$FileName,
                       Rpattern = "TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG")
setwd(oldwd)

proj3 <- qAlign(sampleFile2, genomeFile, maxHits = 50)

mirs <- import("extdata/mirbaseXX_qsr.gff3")
names(mirs) <- mirs$Name
preMirs <- mirs[ mirs$type == "miRNA_primary_transcript" ]
matureMirs <- mirs[ mirs$type == "miRNA" ]

matureMirsExtended <- resize(matureMirs, width = 1L, fix = "start") + 3L

cnt <- qCount(proj3, matureMirsExtended, orientation = "same")
cnt <- qCount(proj3, preMirs, orientation = "same")

workflows.name: bis_seq_workflow
workflows.intent: Align bisulfite-converted reads and quantify DNA methylation levels at single-cytosine resolution or across genomic regions.
input: samples_bis_single.txt (tab-delimited sample file listing bisulfite fasta files)
workflows.stages: 1. Align bisulfite-converted reads using qAlign with bisulfite="dir" or "undir". ;; 2. Quantify methylation states for all genomic CpGs using qMeth. ;; 3. Quantify methylation states across specific query regions (e.g., promoters) using qMeth with collapseByQueryRegion=TRUE.
workflows.code:
file.copy(system.file(package = "QuasR", "extdata"), ".", recursive = TRUE)

sampleFile <- "extdata/samples_bis_single.txt"
genomeFile <- "extdata/hg19sub.fa"

proj4 <- qAlign(sampleFile, genomeFile, bisulfite = "dir")
proj4

meth <- qMeth(proj4, mode = "CpGcomb", collapseBySample = TRUE)

qMeth(proj4, query = GRanges("chr1",IRanges(start = 31633, width = 2)),
      collapseBySample = TRUE)

qMeth(proj4, query = promRegSel, collapseByQueryRegion = TRUE,
      collapseBySample = TRUE)
